title_ar: الشيخ الددو يحاضر لجمعية المستقبل عن "السلوك الحضاري"
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Lectures to the Future Association on "Civilised Conduct"
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو مساء أمس في فضاء التنوع الثقافي بالعاصمة انواكشوط محاضرة بعنوان: "السلوك الحضاري"، تعرض فيها لنقاط مهمة في الموضوع نجملها فيما يلي: 1- اعتناء الإسلام بترسيخ المسلكيات الحضارية المحمودة، ونبذ السلوك الفردي المقيت والمذموم. 2- التزام الإنسان بالأوامر والنواهي يعتبر سلوكا حضاريا وصمام أمان من التخلف والبداوة السلبية. 3- ضمان الله سبحانه وتعالى لبني آدم أصول الحوائج الضرورية، وذلك في قوله تعالى:" إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ فِيهَا وَلا تَعْرَى (118) وَأَنَّكَ لا تَظْمَأُ فِيهَا وَلا تَضْحَى (119)(طه). 4- نبذ عادات الجاهلية الغير حضارية مثل وأد البنات وحداد المرأة سنة كاملة على زوجها .... إلخ. 5- من السلوك الحضاري احترام خصوصيات الآخرين، لقوله تعالى: يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَدْخُلُوا بُيُوتاً غَيْرَ بُيُوتِكُمْ حَتَّى تَسْتَأْنِسُوا وَتُسَلِّمُوا عَلَى أَهْلِهَا ذَلِكُمْ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ (27) (النور) ونشير هنا إلى أن المحاضرة تم تنظيمها من قبل جمعية المستقبل التي يرأسها فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو- حفظه الله- وقد حضرها جمع غفير من محبي الشيخ والمهتمين بالشأن الدعوي رجالا ونساءً، كما حضر هذا النشاط وفد من خيرة شباب ومشايخ دولة الكويت الشقيقة يزور البلاد حاليا للمساهمة في أعمال خيرية ودعوية.
body_en:
His eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew delivered a lecture yesterday evening at the Cultural Diversity Space in the capital, Nouakchott, entitled "Civilised Conduct", in which he dealt with important points on the subject, which we summarise as follows:

1 — Islam's concern to entrench praiseworthy civilised patterns of conduct, and to cast off individual conduct that is odious and blameworthy.

2 — A person's adherence to the commands and the prohibitions is counted a piece of civilised conduct and a safety valve against backwardness and negative bedouinism.

3 — God's guarantee — glorified and exalted is He — to the children of Adam of the roots of their necessary needs, this being in His words, exalted is He: {Truly it is yours that you shall not hunger therein, nor be naked; and that you shall not thirst therein, nor suffer the sun's heat.} (Sūrat Ṭā Hā 20:118–119)

4 — Casting off the uncivilised customs of the age of ignorance, such as the burying of infant girls, and a woman's mourning a full year for her husband .... and so on.

5 — Part of civilised conduct is respecting the privacy of others, in accordance with His words, exalted is He: {O you who believe, do not enter houses other than your own until you have sought leave and greeted their people. That is better for you, that you may be mindful.} (Sūrat al-Nūr 24:27)

We note here that the lecture was organised by the Future Association, which is headed by his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew — may God preserve him — and that it was attended by a great gathering of those who love the Sheikh and of those concerned with the work of calling people to Islam, men and women alike. A delegation of the finest young men and shaykhs of the sisterly State of Kuwait, currently visiting the country to take part in charitable and da'wah work, also attended this event.

flags.context: point 2, on what adherence to the commands and prohibitions guards against
options: the negative side of nomadic life
flags.note: A phrase that reads very differently in English than in Arabic. In the Mauritanian setting 'البداوة' names a specific social and economic formation with recognised positive aspects, and the modifier 'السلبية' exists precisely to restrict the criticism to the negative side of it. A flat English 'bedouinism' reads as disparagement of an ethnic group and would be quotable as such. Translated literally and neither softened nor sharpened, but the phrasing needs a decision before publication, and the reader should be told this is a news summary and not the Sheikh's own wording.

flags.arabic: حداد المرأة سنة كاملة على زوجها
flags.context: point 4, in the list of pre-Islamic customs cast off
options: report it exactly as an abrogated custom of the age of ignorance, as the summary does
gloss it against the Islamic waiting period
flags.note: The item is listed as a pre-Islamic custom that Islam cast off. The English must not be read as a ruling on the waiting period (ʿiddah) in Islamic law, which is a separate matter and is not discussed here. No gloss has been added, because the Sheikh — as summarised — gave none, and supplying one would be adding a legal point he did not make.

flags.context: the framing of the five numbered points
options: keep the reporting frame visible throughout and never present the points as the Sheikh's own words
present the points as direct statements by the Sheikh
flags.note: The site editor states plainly that the five points are his own summary of the lecture, not a transcript. Every point is therefore second-hand. The English keeps the summary frame and the numbered points must not be quoted as the Sheikh's written words. Points 3 and 5 in particular attach scriptural proof-texts to propositions, and whether the Sheikh drew those links in those terms cannot be established from this record.

flags.arabic: عادات الجاهلية الغير حضارية ... " إِنَّ لَكَ أَلاَّ تَجُوعَ
flags.context: two orthographic and punctuation defects in the source
options: leave both as served and record them
flags.note: 'الغير حضارية' uses 'الغير' as a prefixed negator, which is non-standard for 'غير الحضارية'; and the quotation of Ṭā Hā opens with a quotation mark that is never closed, the verse running into the parenthetical sura name. Both are left as served in body_ar per style guide section 11. The English supplies the closing brace and the reference, which is presentation rather than restoration.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh; the reporting frame is preserved throughout.
Qur'anic renderings are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic. The source gives the verse numbers and sura names but not in the corpus format; the references have been regularised.
'جمعية المستقبل' is rendered 'the Future Association' with the Arabic name available in body_ar; the organisation's own English name, if it has one, should be preferred once known.
The four dots in point 4 are the source's own ellipsis before 'and so on', indicating the summariser truncated the list; retained.
